questions.stem: Explain what an ISA guarantees to a compiler writer and why this is important.
markingGuide: An ISA guarantees a consistent set of instructions and addressing modes.
This consistency allows the compiler to generate machine code that will execute correctly on any processor implementing the ISA.
It abstracts the hardware details, allowing software to be portable across different hardware implementations.
questions.explanation: An ISA provides a stable interface for compiler writers, ensuring that the machine code generated will work on any compatible processor. This abstraction is crucial for software portability and efficient compiler design.

questions.stem: A processor uses a 3-bit opcode and has 8 registers. How many different instructions can be encoded using this opcode? Assume each instruction uses one register operand.
questions.explanation: With a 3-bit opcode, there are $2^3 = 8$ possible opcodes. Each opcode can work with 8 different registers, leading to $8 \times 3 = 24$ unique instructions.

questions.stem: Discuss the impact of addressing modes on the performance of a processor.
markingGuide: Different addressing modes require different numbers of memory accesses.
Immediate addressing is fast as it uses constants directly.
Memory addressing may slow down execution due to additional memory accesses.
Register addressing is typically faster than memory addressing as it accesses data directly from registers.
questions.explanation: Addressing modes affect how quickly data can be accessed and manipulated. Immediate addressing is quick because it uses constants, while memory addressing can be slower due to the need for additional memory accesses. Register addressing is generally faster than memory addressing.
